_about: Single declaration of the requirements graph (S-63, kernel page requirements-graph). The sensor reads this file; the kernel page explains it for humans. Edges are written in one direction only; the inverse is computed. Each edge is enforced only from the status declared in 'enforced_from' (lesson of SDD_chain_artifacts_check: checking every pair everywhere produced 366 false positives).

edge_syntax.file_node: YAML frontmatter key in the node's own file: `epic: "[[prd#^EP-01]]"`, lists for many targets
edge_syntax.inline_node: Inline field on the line under the node inside its document: `serves:: [[ROADMAP#^OUT-01]]` (epics in prd.md, releases in ROADMAP.md)
edge_syntax.block_anchor: `^ID` at the end of the paragraph or list item that holds the node (outcomes, releases, observable states); letters, digits and hyphens only

_off_track: valid statuses outside the lifecycle order: never count as reached for enforced_from, never open (MJRP, 2026-10-04 14:28: Deferred joins the rules)

observable_state.note: a situation of the system surface the human sees and judges: a screen state of the judged prototype (info-arch.md, visual surface) or a behavior state (behavior.md, non-visual surface: command output, exit code, generated file, hook block, API response, agent behavior). MJRP, 2026-10-04 14:41: one rule for every requirement, no exemption by project type or by date. A link with a path (apps/<app>/docs/specs/info-arch#^x) resolves in that nested project.

edges.name: planned_for
edges.note: on an epic it is a shortcut for all its requirements; the requirement overrides

edges.name: supersedes
edges.note: required when a Done requirement changes: the change is a new requirement that supersedes the old one

edges.name: delivered_by
edges.note: the commit that delivered a requirement with no Done feature (meta work, or delivered before the graph); evidence for Done

edges.name: accepted_in
edges.note: the human's acceptance: an entry of uat.md ([[uat#^UAT-xx]]) or of the log ('log YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'); evidence for Accepted

constraints.text: a requirement is imported by at most one open feature (MJRP, 2026-10-04: requirement -> feature 0..1 open at a time)
an NFR is never imported by a feature; it constrains all of them and is checked in review with constitution.md
every REQ of a feature is implemented by at least one TASK of the same feature
all requirements imported by one feature are planned for the same release (when the project declares releases)
every edge target resolves: file, heading or block anchor exists
a Done or Accepted requirement has evidence: a Done feature imports it, or delivered_by names a commit that exists
an Accepted requirement has accepted_in pointing to the human's acceptance (uat.md entry or log entry)
an In progress requirement has an open feature, or activity in stale_days (a commit on the node or its feature, or a log entry citing it) — time rule, daily pass
the observable state a Ready requirement points to did not change after the requirement was last touched — time rule, daily pass

a Ready requirement that points to a screen state (info-arch.md, nested included) points to a state an approved prototype shows: the state's block ID is in a shows:: line of the record in § Protótipos aprovados. Behavior states are exempt (MJRP, 2026-10-04)
a Done feature has no open task
requirement files live in the folder their epic declares with folder:: in prd.md (ep-NN-<english-slug>/), NFRs in nfr/; dormant while no epic declares folder:: (S-123, MJRP 2026-10-05)
every node has a non-empty `## <lang>` section for each language in `languages` (S-110)

_evidence: S-67 (MJRP, 2026-10-04): status asks for evidence, one rule for every project — the feature for code-app work, the commit for meta work or work delivered before the graph.
_languages: S-110 (MJRP, 2026-10-05 09:39): every requirement and NFR node carries one `## <lang>` section per language, same file, same ID; the contract's mjrp_harness.requirements.languages overrides ([] turns it off)
_tags: MJRP, 2026-10-06: every outcome carries 1 to 3 category tags (`tags:: #a #b` in its ROADMAP section) and every epic inherits the tags of the outcome it serves and may add up to 3 of its own (`tags::` under its heading in prd.md). Free vocabulary: the sensor checks only the format (English kebab-case after #) and the count.
